description: A multilingual product release is approaching, and the localization team needs a current picture of which strings, screenshots, legal disclaimers, and voice-over assets are actually ready in each target language. All product names are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 32-year-old release localization coordinator responsible for several language tracks
user_profile.context: Everyone says they are almost done, but no one has a trustworthy cross-asset view of what is truly ready
user_profile.communication_style: Status-focused and practical, prefers a clean readiness breakdown over narrative updates

fact_sheet.fact: The final release date for the product 'Project Nimbus v3.0' is scheduled for November 15, 2023.
The code freeze for Project Nimbus v3.0, including all source UI strings, was on October 20, 2023, at 5:00 PM PST.
The final delivery deadline for all localized assets (strings, media, legal) to the build team is November 8, 2023.
The multilingual localization Quality Assurance (QA) cycle is scheduled to begin on November 9, 2023.
The German (de-DE) UI string translation is 100% complete and has passed linguistic review in the LingoHub TMS.
The Japanese (ja-JP) UI string translation is at 98% completion, with 45 strings remaining in the 'Linguistic Review' stage.
The French (fr-FR) UI string translation is at 85% completion, blocked by 12 unresolved terminology questions.
The Spanish (es-ES) UI string translation is 100% complete, but 12 strings are flagged for exceeding character length limits.
The total source word count for Project Nimbus v3.0 UI strings is 24,580 words.
The string key 'error.connection.timeout.message' has 3 open clarification requests from the translation team.
All 215 product screenshots for the German (de-DE) market have been captured and are awaiting final approval from the marketing team.
180 out of 215 product screenshots for the Japanese (ja-JP) market have been captured; the remaining 35 are blocked by UI bug #NIM-7812.
The French (fr-FR) voice-over assets for the onboarding tutorial are complete and have been delivered as 'FR_VO_Tutorial_Final.wav'.
The Spanish (es-ES) voice-over assets are blocked; the selected voice actor, Javier Rios, has a scheduling conflict until November 6, 2023.
The budget allocated for voice-over work is $8,500 USD, of which $4,200 has been spent to date.
The master video file requiring voice-over dubbing is located at '//server/assets/Nimbus_v3/video/onboarding_master_v2.mp4'.
The German (de-DE) legal disclaimer was approved by legal counsel Markus Weber on October 25, 2023.
The Japanese (ja-JP) legal disclaimer is pending review by the regional legal team in Tokyo; the deadline for feedback is November 3, 2023.
The French (fr-FR) legal disclaimer requires an update to comply with DGCCRF regulations; a new draft is expected by EOD November 1, 2023.
The Spanish (es-ES) legal disclaimer was approved on October 28, 2023, and the final text is available in the TMS under key 'legal.disclaimer.es-es'.
The primary Translation Management System (TMS) is LingoHub, accessible at 'https://stellar-innovations.lingohub.com'.
Localized UI string files are managed in the Git repository 'git@github.com:StellarInnovations/nimbus-localization.git' in the 'release/v3.0' branch.
The dedicated Slack channel for all Nimbus v3.0 localization coordination is '#loc-nimbus-v3'.
All localization-related bugs should be filed in Jira under the project key 'NIMLOC' and linked to the master release epic 'NIM-7500'.
The release localization coordinator is Alani Kovač, reachable at 'alani.kovac@stellar-innovations.com' or extension 4482.
The legal counsel responsible for disclaimer approvals is Markus Weber, reachable at 'markus.weber@stellar-innovations.com'.
The lead reviewer for Japanese (ja-JP) translations is Kenji Tanaka, whose LingoHub username is 'ktanaka'.
The primary contact for French (fr-FR) terminology questions is Sophie Dubois, the lead French translator, available on Slack as '@sophie.dubois'.

user_needs.description: What are the final release date, localized-asset delivery deadline, and QA start date for Project Nimbus v3.0?
What is the current status of the German UI strings, product screenshots, and legal disclaimer?
What is the status of the French (fr-FR) UI strings and who do I contact about the terminology blockers?
Are the French voice-over assets ready and where can I find them?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After checking the status of one French asset (strings), the user is likely to ask about other assets for the same language.

user_needs.description: Why is the French legal disclaimer not approved yet?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning about blockers with French strings, the user is likely concerned about other French assets, making the status of the legal disclaimer a logical next question.

user_needs.description: What is holding up the Japanese (ja-JP) UI string translation from being 100% complete?
Who is the lead reviewer for the Japanese translations?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After identifying that strings are stuck in review, the user's immediate next step is to find out who the reviewer is to follow up.

user_needs.description: What is blocking the capture of the remaining Japanese product screenshots?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: While investigating Japanese string issues, the user would be interested in other blockers for the same language, such as the screenshot problem.

user_needs.description: Are there any issues with the Spanish (es-ES) UI strings, even though they are 100% translated?
What is the status of the Spanish voice-over assets?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After checking on Spanish strings, the user will naturally want to know the status of other key Spanish assets like voice-overs.

user_needs.description: How many Spanish UI strings are flagged for exceeding character length limits?
user_needs.prediction_reason: After confirming that the Spanish UI strings are 100% translated but still have issues, a direct follow-up is how many strings are flagged for those character-length problems.
